page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating with dedicated CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core computational capabilities. The instance achieves top 25% performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU physics and encryption tests. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with PassMark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth placing in the top 25%. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth tests fall into the middle 50% average tier.

Given its high compute density and dedicated CPU resources, the c2d-highcpu-56 offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It performs strongly in software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. It is also capable of handling small to medium LLM inference tasks, though performance scales down to average tiers for larger 70B models. This profile makes it highly suitable for high-performance computing, CI/CD pipelines, and compute-heavy web serving.
